faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.description: Answers to common questions about Sailock, how it works, and how to get started.

whatIs.question: What is Sailock?
whatIs.answer: Sailock is a local-first password manager for Windows. It keeps your encrypted vault stored on your own device — there's no cloud account and no server involved.

isFree.question: Is Sailock free?
isFree.answer: Yes. Sailock is free and open source. You can use it, inspect its source code, and contribute to it without any cost.

whereDownload.question: Where can I download Sailock?
whereDownload.answer: You can download the latest version from the official GitHub repository or from the Microsoft Store.

windows.question: Is Sailock available for other platforms besides Windows?
windows.answer: Right now Sailock is built specifically for Windows. Support for other platforms isn't planned in the short term, but community feedback is welcome.

offline.question: Does Sailock work without an internet connection?
offline.answer: Yes. Sailock works fully offline. Your vault lives on your device, so an internet connection isn't required to use it.

openSource.question: Is Sailock open source?
openSource.answer: Yes. The full source code is available on GitHub under an open license, and anyone is welcome to review it or contribute.

security.question: How does Sailock protect my passwords?
security.answer: Your vault is encrypted with AES-256, and access is protected by your master password. Sailock also supports TOTP-based two-factor authentication for an extra layer of security.

masterPassword.question: What happens if I forget my master password?
masterPassword.answer: Because Sailock doesn't store your master password anywhere, if you lose it there's no way to recover access to your vault. Make sure to keep it somewhere safe.
